items.review_rationale: Read the entire length-based valuation construction on nonzero elements of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, distinguishing quotient-module length from prime-chain length and extending to fraction ratios with subtraction.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient of R by principal ideal generated by a nonzero element

references.disposition: The formula extends the assigned order from nonzero R-elements to K× using differences of module lengths; it does not assert every fractional element is in R.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the categorical cancellation test using post-composition with arbitrary g,h:S→T and the equivalent multiplication-map criterion on S⊗_R S; ring epimorphisms need not be set-surjective.

references.phrase: multiplication map S⊗_R S→S is ring isomorphism
references.context: Commutative algebra: multiplication morphism of the tensor-product R-algebra and an isomorphism of commutative rings

references.phrase: g∘f=h∘f implies g=h for all g,h
references.disposition: Cancellation is tested for all commutative target rings T and maps out of S, not ordinary surjectivity of f.

items.review_rationale: Read the three defining conditions of a filtered category: nonemptiness, common targets of pairs of objects, and eventual equalization of parallel arrows. This is not just a directed preorder, although directed preorders are special cases.

references.context: Category theory: two morphisms in the same category with equal source and target
Category theory: existence of a cocone over two indexing objects

references.phrase: after an arrow j→k, u and v become equal
references.disposition: The specified equalization of parallel arrows is a separate requirement from a common upper object; all three axioms are present.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the filtered-colimit meaning in arbitrary category C together with its specialized Sets description, distinguishing the colimit universal property from the eventual identification relation on elements.

references.phrase: colimit of a diagram of sets
become equal at some later common stage
references.context: Set theory and category theory: equivalence of representatives under forward transition maps in a filtered diagram

references.disposition: The eventual equality description refers to set-valued diagrams and is not an elementwise definition valid in every category C.

items.review_rationale: Read the specified 2-commutative square, invertible 2-morphisms, diagonal fillers, and compatible modifications between fillers; retained the (2,1)-category setting rather than replacing it with ordinary commuting squares.

references.context: Higher category theory: square of 1-morphisms equipped with specified invertible comparison 2-cell
Higher category theory: filler of a given 2-commutative square satisfying compatibility equations

references.disposition: Arrows in this filler category must commute with the specified 2-cell data, not arbitrary isomorphisms of its ambient objects.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the exact order duality: cofiltered means filtered opposite category; common arrows now come from a common object and parallel arrows are equalized after precomposition, not postcomposition.

references.phrase: nonempty and any two objects receive arrows from a common source
references.disposition: Direction is reversed from filteredness; existence alone does not entail the parallel-arrow axiom.

references.phrase: parallel arrows become equal after precomposition
references.disposition: Equalization takes place by precomposing with an arrow into their common source.

items.review_rationale: Read geometric connectedness as connectedness of Spec(A⊗_k K) after every field extension K/k, not merely connectedness of Spec(A) or geometric irreducibility.

references.phrase: k-algebra A and its scalar-extension K-algebra
references.context: Commutative algebra: algebra over field k and scalar extension with induced K-algebra multiplication

references.disposition: All extensions are allowed, including transcendental ones; no Noetherian or finite type hypothesis is supplied.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed inverse limit of a diagram of topological spaces as compatible point families inside its product, with the inherited subspace topology; did not confuse an inverse limit with an unrestricted product.

references.context: Category theory and topology: element tuples satisfying all transition-map compatibility equations in inverse system

references.disposition: The subset is restricted by the diagram equations and is not the entire topological product in general.
